{
  "subtype": "faceted_decomposition",
  "concept": "airline_competitive_advantage",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "crew_friendliness_warmth",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "The warmth/friendliness of cabin crew is a genuine sub-aspect OF an airline's service offering, which is itself a pillar of competitive advantage. It is an attribute of the concept, not an external driver of it."
    },
    {
      "name": "crew_attentiveness_responsiveness",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Attentiveness/responsiveness of crew is a distinct in-flight service dimension and thus a constitutive aspect of competitive advantage. It overlaps somewhat with crew_friendliness (both are 'cabin crew service'), but captures a different behavioural axis (helpfulness/speed vs. warmth)."
    },
    {
      "name": "seat_comfort_legroom",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Seat comfort and legroom is a hard-product/cabin dimension along which airlines compete, i.e. an aspect OF the competitive advantage, not a predictor of it."
    },
    {
      "name": "food_beverage_quality",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Catering quality is a recognised service/product dimension that partly constitutes an airline's advantage; it is a part-of aspect of the concept."
    },
    {
      "name": "ground_staff_service",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Ground service (check-in, gate, handling) is a distinct service touchpoint and a legitimate constitutive facet of the overall competitive advantage, non-overlapping with in-flight crew touchpoints."
    }
  ],
  "facet_columns": [
    "crew_friendliness_warmth",
    "crew_attentiveness_responsiveness",
    "seat_comfort_legroom",
    "food_beverage_quality",
    "ground_staff_service"
  ],
  "non_facet_columns": [],
  "mutual_exclusivity": 0.8,
  "exhaustiveness": 0.55,
  "rationale": "All five added columns are genuine part-of aspects of an airline's competitive advantage (service warmth, service responsiveness, seat/hardware comfort, catering, ground service) rather than external predictors, causes, or restatements, so the part-of/meronymy claim is satisfied. Mutual exclusivity is high but not perfect: the two crew columns (friendliness vs. attentiveness) both live under the 'cabin crew service' aspect and can co-vary, and crew vs. ground staff both fall under the broader 'service' banner, creating mild redundancy risk. Exhaustiveness is only moderate: the set carves the 'service + comfort + food' portion of competitive advantage well, but omits several major constitutive facets of airline competitive advantage such as price/value-for-money, inflight entertainment, on-time performance/reliability, network/route connectivity, baggage handling, and boarding/check-in efficiency. Because it covers roughly half of the concept's constitutive dimensions, exhaustiveness is scored around 0.55."
}
